sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Section CCXXVII ("taking up that celestial and first of bows created by Brahma of old and called Gandiva, Arjuna was filled with joy")

note.en: Varuna gives Arjuna the bow Gandiva during the Khandava-daha episode

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Section CCXXVII ("the lord Varuna gave unto Krishna a mace of name Kaumodaki")
Bhishma Parva, Section XXV ("Hrishikesha blew (the conch called) Pancajanya")
Sabha Parva, Section XLV (Krishna "cut off the head of the ruler of Chedi by means of his discus")
Vana Parva, Section XL ("I will give to thee that favourite weapon of mine called the Pasuputa. O son of Pandu, thou art capable of holding, hurling, and withdrawing it")

note.en: Shiva gives Arjuna the Pashupatastra after being pleased by his penance and prowess
Rama breaks the bow (identified as Shiva's Pinaka in this account) at Sita's swayamvara at Mithila

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Sarga 67 (1-67-17: "the foremost man broke that bow medially while examining its bowstring's tautness")

note.en: The bow kept and venerated by Janaka's line, broken by Rama at the swayamvara, is identified as Shiva's own

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section XXI ("the bow Sharanga dropped from my hand")
Sabha Parva, Section XLV (Shiva described as "armed with the trident and the bow called Pinaka")
Sabha Parva, Section XLV (Shiva described as "armed with the trident and the bow called Pinaka")

note.en: Sharanga is traditionally Vishnu's bow, wielded by him in his incarnation as Krishna

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section XXI (Krishna wields the bow Sharanga)
Karna Parva, Section 89 ("the suta's son Karna of great valour shot in that encounter the varunastra for quenching it")

note.en: Karna quenches Arjuna's fire weapon with the Varunastra during their Kurukshetra combat
Ashvatthama's Narayanastra is pacified only when Bhima is dragged down from his car and made to lay aside his weapons: "the Narayana weapon, that scorcher of foes, became pacified"
Krishna counsels Bhima to lay down his weapons and dismount, pacifying the Narayanastra: "do thou also come down from thy car"

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CCI ("The valiant Aswatthaman...touched water and invoked the Agneya weapon incapable of being resisted by the very gods")

note.en: Arjuna counters Ashvatthama's Agneyastra by invoking the Brahma weapon, "capable of baffling every other weapon"
